cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: test coverage sits at 31%, there is no coverage gate in continuous integration, and production systems of comparable complexity typically run 40-60% coverage.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no coverage gate in continuous integration. Production systems of comparable complexity typically run 40 to 60% coverage. A regression can reach production unchallenged, since no automated control blocks a commit below the benchmark. This gap exposes customers to preventable defects.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: deployments are performed manually by one engineer via SSH, there is no rollback procedure, and the last rollback attempt (8 months ago) took over 3 hours to complete.
cases.output: Deployments are performed manually by a single engineer via SSH with no documented rollback procedure. The most recent rollback attempt, eight months ago, required over three hours to complete, indicating that reverting a failed deployment would extend downtime significantly and remain dependent on one person's availability. This creates a single point of failure for both forward and reverse operations, with no compensating control. A regression or misconfiguration deployed to production has no rapid mitigation path.

evidence_before_interpretation.detail: first sentence contains no concrete figure, expected one for this case's facts: 'Deployments are performed manually by a single engineer via SSH with no documented rollback procedure.'

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: one engineer holds sole access to the production database credentials, there is no documented access-handover process, and that engineer is on a rolling month-to-month contract.
cases.output: The production database credentials are held by a single engineer with no documented handover process, and that engineer works on a rolling month-to-month contract. If the engineer leaves without notice, the company loses access to its production data until credentials can be rotated—a process that has not been tested and carries unknown lead time. There is no compensating control. We recommend establishing a credential vault with at least two named operators, documenting the full handover sequence, and running a dry-run retrieval quarterly to confirm the documented process works.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no deletion policy, and there is no documented process for handling a data-subject deletion request.
cases.output: Customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no documented deletion policy. The company lacks a defined process for handling data-subject deletion requests under applicable privacy regulations. This creates exposure to regulatory penalties and potential customer claims, with no compensating control. A retention schedule and deletion workflow should be implemented before the next customer intake cycle.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) covering ALL of these facts: test coverage is 31%, there is no CI coverage gate, the last three production incidents were caused by untested edge cases, deployments are manual, and there is no rollback procedure. Do not omit any fact.
cases.output: Test coverage across the codebase sits at 31%, with no automated gate preventing low-coverage code from reaching production. Three of the last four production incidents stemmed directly from untested edge cases that passed through manual deployments unchallenged. The deployment process itself is entirely manual, and there is no documented rollback procedure if an incident occurs in production. Together these facts mean that a regression can reach customers without detection, and the team has no systematic path to recover once it does.

cases.input: Write three separate due-diligence findings, one paragraph each, clearly separated by a blank line. Finding 1 facts: passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table. Finding 2 facts: deployments are manual with no rollback procedure. Finding 3 facts: code comment style is inconsistent across the codebase, with no linting rule enforcing a convention.
cases.output:
Passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table. No hashing algorithm is applied before storage, which means that anyone with database access can read credentials in clear text. This exposes every user account to immediate compromise if the database is breached, and it prevents the company from claiming reasonable security posture to customers or regulators.

Deployments are performed manually with no rollback procedure documented or tested. When a deployment fails or introduces a regression, the team must manually revert changes, which extends downtime and increases the window during which customers see errors. A single bad deployment has caused production outages lasting hours; formalized rollback steps would reduce that window to minutes.

Code comments follow no consistent style, and no linting rule enforces a convention. New developers spend time deciphering comment formats instead of understanding the logic they document. Standardizing the convention and adding an automated check would improve onboarding velocity and make the codebase easier to maintain as it grows.
